name: Lunokhod 2
def: Second Soviet lunar rover, delivered by Luna 21 to Le Monnier crater, which drove roughly 39 kilometres in under four months.
body: Lunokhod 2 landed on 15 January 1973 and explored the boundary between Le Monnier crater and the Taurus mountains, driving faster than its predecessor thanks to a third television camera and an improved navigation system. Power came from a lid mounted solar panel with a polonium 210 heater for the lunar night, turning the same eight wheel chassis. It surveyed the local magnetic field and a nearby rille before its open lid scooped dust onto the radiator in May 1973, causing the rover to overheat.
facts: Held the off world driving record for four decades
Agreed traverse of about 39 km, re estimated near 42 km from orbital imagery
Carried a French laser retroreflector still used for ranging
specs: Eight independently driven wheels with individual motors and brakes
Lid mounted solar panel with polonium 210 radioisotope heater
Three television cameras, panoramic telephotometers, boom mounted magnetometer, photodetector, solar X ray experiment, laser retroreflector
Teleoperated from Earth using television guidance
